nodes.description: Basement membranes fail to form or are structurally abnormal. In the mouse this is lethal in embryogenesis when glucosyltransferase activity is low enough; in surviving humans it is the substrate of the multisystem phenotype. In one patient the failure extended to the dermal-epidermal junction, with sub-lamina-densa blistering, abnormal anchoring fibrils and markedly reduced type VII collagen despite a normal COL7A1.
nodes.id: Basement Membrane and Extracellular Matrix Failure

evidence.reference_title: Glycosylation catalyzed by lysyl hydroxylase 3 is essential for basement membranes.
evidence.snippet: the reduction of the GGT activity of LH3 disrupts the localization of type IV collagen, and thus the formation of basement membranes during mouse embryogenesis leading to lethality at embryonic day (E) 9.5-14.5

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PLOD3, encoding lysyl hydroxylase 3, cause a complex connective tissue disorder including recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa-like blistering phenotype with abnormal anchoring fibrils and type VII collagen deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The blistering in the skin occurred below the lamina densa and was associated with variable density and morphology of anchoring fibrils. The level of type VII collagen expression in the skin was markedly reduced.

nodes.description: Type VI collagen fails to tetramerise inside the cell, and both type IV and type VI collagen are secreted poorly. The defect is therefore in getting the collagen out, not only in how it behaves once outside. Mice retaining glycosylation but lacking the lysyl hydroxylase activity make slightly underglycosylated type IV and VI collagens with abnormal distribution, and their muscle ultrastructure resembles collagen VI knockouts and some Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy patients.

evidence.reference_title: Secretion and assembly of type IV and VI collagens depend on glycosylation of hydroxylysines.
evidence.snippet: The altered distribution and aggregation of type VI collagen led to similar ultrastructural alterations in muscle to those detected in collagen VI knockout and some Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy patients.

readouts.interpretation: Direct measurement of the glycosylation node: the reaction product LH3 is responsible for is the analyte.

nodes.description: Collagen hydroxylysines are left without their galactosyl and glucosylgalactosyl sugars. This is the step that matters: a mouse blocked only in the lysyl hydroxylase activity develops normally, while reducing the glucosyltransferase activity is embryonic-lethal in proportion to how much activity is lost. In patients the deficit is measurable, as markedly reduced glycosylated hydroxylysine in tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Glycosylation catalyzed by lysyl hydroxylase 3 is essential for basement membranes.
evidence.snippet: Mice with a mutation that blocked only the LH activity of LH3 developed normally, but showed defects in the structure of the basement membrane and in collagen fibril organization in newborn skin and lung.

evidence.reference_title: Glycosylation catalyzed by lysyl hydroxylase 3 is essential for basement membranes.
evidence.snippet: survival of hypomorphic embryos and the formation of the basement membrane were directly correlated with the level of GGT activity

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PLOD3, encoding lysyl hydroxylase 3, cause a complex connective tissue disorder including recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa-like blistering phenotype with abnormal anchoring fibrils and type VII collagen deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of hydroxylysine and its glycosylated derivatives (galactosyl-hydroxylysine and glucosyl-galactosyl-hydroxylysine) revealed marked reduction in glycosylated hydroxylysine.

nodes.description: The clinical syndrome. Tissues dependent on basement membrane and network collagen integrity fail across the body, with the distribution mirroring where LH3 is expressed in development: cochlea, eyes, skin, forelimbs, heart and cartilage.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in PLOD3 result in a Stickler syndrome-like connective tissue disorder with vascular complications.
evidence.snippet: Human lysyl hydroxylase 3/PLOD3 expression was localised to the developing cochlea, eyes, skin, forelimbs, heart and cartilage, mirroring the clinical phenotype of this disorder.

nodes.description: Biallelic PLOD3 variants reduce LH3 enzyme activity and, in reported patients, LH3 protein levels in cells and skin. Individual alleles can selectively knock out either the glycosyltransferase or the lysyl hydroxylase site, which is what makes the separation of the two activities clinically as well as experimentally meaningful.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PLOD3, encoding lysyl hydroxylase 3, cause a complex connective tissue disorder including recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa-like blistering phenotype with abnormal anchoring fibrils and type VII collagen deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The level of LH3 was dramatically reduced in the skin and fibroblast cultures from the patient.
